pr_title: Fix Equals overload logic for some methods of an array created using MLC
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/57728
Update Equals overload for RoMethods created by MetadataLoadContext to check `ReturnType` instead of `DeclaringType`

issue_context.title: Some MethodInfo(s) of array types loaded by MetadataLoadContext are incorrectly evaluated as equal.
issue_context.body:
### Description

Some MethodInfo(s) of array types loaded by MetadataLoadContext are incorrectly evaluated as equal.
They are expected not to be equal.

```
        [Fact]
        public void MethodsShouldBeDistinguished()
        {
            using var context = new MetadataLoadContext(new PathAssemblyResolver(Directory.EnumerateFiles(RuntimeEnvironment.GetRuntimeDirectory(), "*.dll").Append(typeof(ArrayTests).Assembly.Location)));
            Type project(Type x) => context.LoadFromAssemblyName(x.Assembly.FullName).GetType(x.FullName, true);
17          void test(Type type) => Assert.NotEqual(type.GetMethod("Get"), type.GetMethod("Set"));
            test(typeof(int[]));
19          test(project(typeof(int[])));
        }
```

```
  Failed MLCTests.ArrayTests.MethodsShouldBeDistinguished [54 ms]
  Error Message:
   Assert.NotEqual() Failure
Expected: Not System.Int32 Get(System.Int32)
Actual:   System.Void Set(System.Int32, System.Int32)
  Stack Trace:
     at MLCTests.ArrayTests.<MethodsShouldBeDistinguished>g__test|0_1(Type type) in .../MLCTests/ArrayTests.cs:line 17
   at MLCTests.ArrayTests.MethodsShouldBeDistinguished() in .../MLCTests/ArrayTests.cs:line 19
```

[MLCTests.tar.gz](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/files/7014561/MLCTests.tar.gz)

### Configuration

* System.Reflection.MetadataLoadContext      5.0.1

```
$ LANG=C dotnet --info
.NET SDK (reflecting any global.json):
 Version:   6.0.100-preview.5.21302.13
 Commit:    d6380bcae7

Runtime Environment:
 OS Name:     arch
 OS Version:  
 OS Platform: Linux
 RID:         arch-x64
 Base Path:   .../sdk/6.0.100-preview.5.21302.13/

Host (useful for support):
  Version: 6.0.0-preview.5.21301.5
  Commit:  ec3e0b276b
```

### Other information

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/57bfe474518ab5b7cfe6bf7424a79ce3af9d6657/src/libraries/System.Reflection.MetadataLoadContext/src/System/Reflection/TypeLoading/Types/RoArrayType.cs#L150

In the above method, Get, Set, and Address can have same `uniquifier`  between calls.
I think `uniquifier` should be consistent for a MetadataLoadContext instance.

I see, looks like a bug

Caused from the `Equals` override in `RoSyntheticMethod`
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a4894885a534c3c9091fd7dedae18d2686c6b844/src/libraries/System.Reflection.MetadataLoadContext/src/System/Reflection/TypeLoading/Methods/RoSyntheticMethod.cs#L70-L82
Probably we need to also check the method name for equality what you think @steveharter

>Probably we need to also check the method name for equality what you think @steveharter

Although that would fix it, that would also impact perf.

I think the bug in this case is that the Equals method should check `_returnType`  instead of `DeclaringType`. DeclaringType will always be the same (`RoArrayType`).

FWIW the hard-coded values for "Get", "Set" and "Address" are there because these are special cases so they have to be manually added via "synthetic method".

> I think the bug in this case is that the Equals method should check _returnType instead of DeclaringType. DeclaringType will always be the same (RoArrayType).

That makes sense, thank you!

> Look carefully at 'Other information' of the issue.

Oops, sorry did not notice that

> An easy way would be to assign constant uniquifiers to Get/Set/Address.

If that is the case then the `uniquifier` is redundant, doesn't seem we need that at all
cc: @steveharter PTAL regarding the need of `uniquifier`

> An easy way would be to assign constant uniquifiers to Get/Set/Address.
>> If that is the case then the uniquifier is redundant, doesn't seem we need that at all

Although currently `uniquifier` is not needed due to adding the `ReturnType` in the last PR (which by coincidence is unique across the 3 methods), keeping the `uniquifier`, but making it hard-coded instead (e.g. 0=Get; 1=Set; 2=Address) would still be good to make the code more clear and consistent with the other areas that use `uniquifier`. Currently since it is incremental it is broken.

Also, if we change to hard-coded `uniquifier`, do we still need `ReturnType`? (I haven't looked at the code again).

> keeping the uniquifier, but making it hard-coded instead

That is even better as do not need the ReturnType check anymore

review_comments: Can you also add a test that verifies Get\Set\Address for `int[]` is not equal to the ones in `long[]`. Thanks.
Good point, that is failing for `Set`, apparently, we need to check `DeclaringType` too

For the current code, is DeclaringType always the same for every RoSyntheticMethod? It should be RoArrayType. In any case, comparing Declaring type as-is makes sense if RoSyntheticMethod is ever used outside of arrays.
Yes `DeclaringType` is always same for every RoSyntheticMethod, need to check it as-is for different array types like `int[]` vs `long[]`
